newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open mixed to lower.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open mixed to lower.

text.p: The Australian stock market opened mixed to slightly lower in patchy pre-weeked trade on Friday, taking its lead from the U.S. market.

"Most leaders are down a little bit," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse Ltd. "The relative weakness of Wall Street would probably have something to do with it ... here is not much inspiration out there at the moment."

The All Ordinaries index was down 11.9 points at 2,723.2 at 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT). Most blue chips lost ground, with the Broken Hill losing 10 cents to A$18.40 and WMC coming down 7.6 cents to A$7.71. Rio Tinto fell 17.7 cents to A$20.70.

Among the big banks, ANZ fell three cents to A$10.70, National Australia was steady at A$19.54 and Westpac lost 2.3 cents to A$8.27. Qantas Airways dipped 3.6 percent to A$2.94 in relatively active early trade.
Dealers said the stock was hurt by rumours that Brian Grey, founder of the failed Compass Airlines, has the backing of some overseas airlines to start up a competing Australian airline.
James Hardie Industries fell three cents to A$4.40.

At the annual meeting on Thursday, the company said it saw a significantly higher profit in 1997/98 but expected a smaller proportion of franking credits to apply to dividend payments in future years.

Oil Search fell another four cents to A$4.18 after the oil producer and explorer said on Thursday that its share of crude oil output from the Kutubu oilfield in Papua New Guinea decreased in the 1997 second quarter.
Gold stocks were mixed after the bullion price fell in New York before it stabilised in Asian trading this morning. Index heavyweight Normandy Mining rose one cent to A$1.56.
